boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Clark's Mill record (November 7, 1862) in Operations North of Boston Mountains [August-November 1862]. The pursuit sent after the Confederates is context. The live NPS campaign label ("Confederate Offensive North of Boston Mountains") does not replace the frozen campaign. Campaign-wide totals, marches and multi-action loss figures are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives about 100 men of the 10th Illinois Cavalry and State Militia against a cavalry brigade of about 1,000; the frozen numeric bounds are 113 for the Union (equal to the frozen Union casualty figure) and 1,000 for the Confederates; the live field reads zero. Wickersham reports about 50 of the 10th Illinois and 50 militia against 1,000. Barstow says he had not more than 110 men against 1,750 cavalry and infantry with four 6-pounders, that he first ascertained the enemy was not less than 1,000, and that they had ten men to his one; he had sent out detachments of 20 and 18 men that morning.
claims.rationale: Two Union reports, one relayed before the other; the frozen Union numeric bound does not match its text. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Barstow sent one detachment toward Gainesville and led another south to reconnoiter; given ten minutes by the Confederate summons, he and his officers judged they could not hold another hour. The Confederate objective is not stated in the inspected passages; Wickersham reports that they burned the block-house and left southward.
claims.rationale: Stated decisions from Union reports; the Confederate aim is unknown in the inspected sources.

claims.value: The frozen rows list Burbridge and Greene (Colonels) for the Confederates and Barstow (Captain) for the Union; the live page names Barstow and Burbridge. Barstow says the commanding colonel gave his name as J. Q. Burbridge, with Greene second in command, and that he decided to surrender after consulting his officers. Wickersham says the enemy was under 'General Green'.
claims.rationale: Accounts differ on the Confederate commander; no listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results are Confederate victory. Wickersham reports the surrender after firing from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m.; Barstow says he surrendered on a demand under a white flag and that the enemy agreed to parole all on the ground. The live description says Barstow surrendered to Burbridge and Greene.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: Frozen: total unknown (US 113; CS unknown). Live: 153 total (US 119; CS 34). Wickersham gives 2 killed and 2 wounded, and 8 enemy killed. Barstow gives 2 killed and 2 wounded in his morning skirmish, with 9 enemy killed, and for the day 7 killed and 2 wounded against 34 enemy killed and a number wounded; the rest of his command was paroled.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Wickersham's figures match Barstow's morning skirmish, not his totals; the live CS 34 equals Barstow's enemy killed (an observation). The frozen US 113 is not found in the inspected passages.
